run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-100a had issues on November 21, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: Between about 13:49:24 and 14:44:44 UTC on 2026-11-21 the payment-api application in namespace app-100a (log stream labels service=payment-api, job=payment-api, pod_name=payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-98kcz) logged database connection-pool exhaustion and 503 responses on its /healthz check. Its own DEBUG lines show the same query, "SELECT * FROM payments WHERE status = ?", taking 15–88 ms in ten samples from 11:21:45 to 13:34:45 and then 1252–4953 ms in five samples from 13:50:55 to 14:43:57, and the error lines report pool_size 20 with active_connections 20 and wait_time_ms up to 26789 ms. Per individual log messages the payload errors were: 13 x "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted", 6 x "ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use" (error_code DB_CONN_001) and 3 x "Health check failed - database unreachable" (status_code 503) over 13:00–17:00, while 21 "Payment processed successfully" lines still appear in that window, so the pod kept serving some requests. No ERROR lines were returned for 12:00–13:49:24 or for 14:50–16:00, and a later sample at 22:52:05 shows an 85 ms database query and a successful payment, so the condition had cleared. The workload and its dependency could not be examined at the pod or metric level: the only payment-api pod now present started 2026-11-22T10:52:40 (after the incident) with 0 restarts and no previous container, no database pod or Service exists in any namespace of this cluster, and every Prometheus and Jaeger call returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. The evidence therefore supports an external database dependency degrading at ~13:45–13:50 as the immediate cause of the payment-api errors, but the worker that owns that database is not present in the evidence, so no root-cause object can be named.

claims.text: The app-100a log stream for service=payment-api shows its first error of the day at 2026-11-21T13:49:24Z: "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted" with pool_size 20, active_connections 20, waiting_requests 27 and wait_time_ms 17653; at 13:50:55 another line reports pool_size 20 / active 20 / waiting 34 / 19706 ms plus "ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use" (error_code DB_CONN_001).

A query for ERROR lines in app-100a from 2026-11-21T12:00:00Z to 13:52:00Z returned exactly three lines, all dated 13:49:24–13:50:55; nothing earlier in that window was returned, so the error burst had not begun before 13:49.

A 5-minute count_over_time of app-100a lines by level shows the ERROR series first becoming non-zero (value 1) at 13:49:46Z and staying non-zero through about 14:49Z, while DEBUG and INFO series exist before that point.

Over 2026-11-21T13:00:00Z–17:00:00Z the app-100a stream contained by message: 13 "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted", 6 "ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use", 3 "Health check failed - database unreachable", 21 "Payment processed successfully", 25 "Database query executed", 25 "Cache operation" and 9 "User authenticated".

The last error lines of the burst are at 2026-11-21T14:44:44Z ("Health check failed - database unreachable", endpoint /healthz, status_code 503, response_time_ms 6354) and 14:43:57Z (pool exhausted, active_connections 20, waiting_requests 21, wait_time_ms 26789); the error lines between 14:01:50 and 14:44:44 are six pool/connection-pool lines and three health-check 503 lines.

Before the burst, ten "Database query executed" lines for "SELECT * FROM payments WHERE status = ?" between 11:21:45 and 13:34:45 report duration_ms of 75, 65, 76, 57, 30, 61, 18, 88, 15 and 65 (rows_returned 93–10).

After the burst began, the same query reports duration_ms 1252 (13:50:55, 98 rows), 3106 (14:28:27, 70 rows), 4953 (14:30:57, 62 rows), 4472 (14:37:32, 24 rows) and 2355 (14:43:57, 30 rows), i.e. roughly 15–300x the pre-13:45 samples for the same statement.
The same stream records /healthz failures with status_code 503 and message "Health check failed - database unreachable" at 13:57:29 (response_time_ms 5009), 14:01:50 (9684) and 14:44:44 (6354).
Later on the same day the stream returns to baseline: at 22:52:05 a "Database query executed" line reports duration_ms 85 (14 rows) alongside "Payment processed successfully".

Log-line volume was 44 lines over the 150 minutes 11:19–13:49 and 42 lines over the 56 minutes 13:49–14:45, i.e. about 0.29 vs 0.75 lines/min, and 22 of the 42 later lines were error lines counted separately.

The only payment-api pod now in app-100a is payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-98kcz, Running/Ready, restartCount 0 with no lastState, started 2026-11-22T10:52:40Z (after the incident), owned by ReplicaSet payment-api-100a-64dcc58445.

Deployment payment-api-100a (namespace app-100a) shows 1 desired / 1 ready / 1 available replica, metadata generation 1 and deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 1, container image python:3.9-slim with command python /app/app-direct-push.py, memory limit 256Mi, liveness probe httpGet /healthz:8080 with failureThreshold 3 and periodSeconds 10, and its app script comes from a Secret volume named in the spec (the Secret contents are redacted and unreadable).

Only two ReplicaSets exist in app-100a — loki-66445c6d6f (created 2026-11-22T10:52:14Z) and payment-api-100a-64dcc58445 (created 2026-11-22T10:52:40Z, image python:3.9-slim, owned by Deployment payment-api-100a) — so no earlier payment-api ReplicaSet is retained to show a template change around 13:45.

All 14 events returned for the authorized window carry timestamps only between 2026-11-22T10:07:47Z and 10:52:41Z: Normal Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started and ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate plus Deployment ScalingReplicaSet "from 0 to 1" for loki and payment-api-100a, and two Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint (service app-100a/loki and app-219/mariadb, "endpoints already exists").

No database workload or database Service exists in this cluster: app-100a contains only the loki and payment-api pods, the cluster-wide pod list (34 pods in app-100a, kube-system, local-path-storage, otel-demo) contains no database pod, and the Service list contains no database Service (app-100a has only loki:3100; there is no Service for payment-api itself).

Most consistent explanation: payment-api's database dependency degraded around 13:45–13:50 (same statement going from 15–88 ms to 1.25–4.95 s, "database unreachable"), which held all 20 pooled connections busy (active_connections 20, wait_time_ms up to 26.8 s) and produced the pool-exhaustion errors and /healthz 503 responses until about 14:44; the cause inside that database cannot be seen because it is not a Kubernetes object in this cluster and no metric or trace source was reachable.

Second candidate, not excluded: the fixed pool_size 20 is simply too small for the offered load, so a moderate request increase exhausted it; the log-line rate rose only from 0.29 to 0.75 lines/min and 20 of the 42 later lines were non-error, which weakens but cannot rule out a load-driven saturation because log lines are not a request count.

Pod crash, OOMKill or eviction as the mechanism is not supported: the payment-api container's restartCount is 0 with an empty lastState and the pod is Ready, and none of the returned events is an OOMKilled, Evicted, Failed or Unhealthy event (the returned events are only the 2026-11-22 10:07–10:52 startup/create/scale set). This rejects a pod-level crash as observed now, though the retained objects postdate the incident.

The pod was not fully down during the burst: 21 "Payment processed successfully" lines appear in 13:00–17:00 with processing_time_ms in the few-hundred-ms range, so the failure was intermittent rather than a total outage of the payment-api service.

Obtain the database's own metrics and logs (server-side max_connections, wait events, slow-query log, host saturation) for 13:40–15:00 UTC on 2026-11-21 to identify what made it slow; that worker is outside this cluster and was not observable here.

Restore metric and trace observability for this workload before re-testing (Prometheus and Jaeger answered SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE throughout the run), and consider a pool/queue timeout and pool-size review for payment-api, since waits of 5–27 s preceded /healthz 503 responses that the liveness probe (failureThreshold 3, periodSeconds 10) would act on.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable in this run: every metrics call (get_metric_names, metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query) returned status error / SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so app_payment_transactions_total, traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_* and kube-state-metrics series could not be read; there is no metric confirmation of the error rate, latency percentile or the pod's restart/availability history.
Jaeger was unavailable: traces_list_services and both traces_search calls returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no trace could confirm which payment-api operations failed or how long callers waited.

The database that payment-api uses is not a Kubernetes object here (no database pod in any namespace, no database Service, namespaces limited to app-100a, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly, otel-demo), so its own state — saturation, connection limit, restarts or configuration change — is unobservable and the root-cause object cannot be named.
The application configuration (database endpoint, pool size) is carried in a Secret-referenced volume that cannot be read, so a configuration change at ~13:45 cannot be verified or excluded.

Kubernetes state postdates the incident: the payment-api pod and its ReplicaSet were created 2026-11-22T10:52:40Z, the deployment is generation/revision 1, and only one ReplicaSet exists, so pod/deployment/ConfigMap state at 13:45 on 2026-11-21 is unknown.
Events survive only from 2026-11-22T10:07:47Z onward; no event between 13:45 and 14:45 on 2026-11-21 was returned (events expire), so the incident-time event history is unknown.
Pod stdout/stderr was empty for the current container payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-98kcz (0 lines read) and there is no previous instance, so container logs could not corroborate the Loki lines.

Loki's log labels carry pod_name=payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-98kcz for 2026-11-21 lines although that pod's kube start time is 2026-11-22T10:52:40Z, so the log-to-pod identity mapping for the incident window is unverified.
Queries for networkpolicies and resourcequotas returned no data, so their absence is not established and they remain unchecked as alternative causes.

A query for ERROR lines across 14:45 on 2026-11-21 to 10:53 on 2026-11-22 timed out, so no complete no-recurrence statement can be made beyond the checked 14:50–16:00 and 15:00–18:00 intervals with the 22:52:05 sample.
The change_history integration is not configured, so no deployment or configuration change record is available for 2026-11-21 13:45.
next_steps: Pull the database server's own logs and metrics (connections, max_connections, lock waits, slow queries, host CPU/IO) for 2026-11-21 13:40–15:00 UTC.
Check whether the payment-api Secret-based configuration (DB host/port, pool size, acquire timeout) was modified before 13:45 UTC on 2026-11-21.
Restore or repair the Prometheus and Jaeger integration for target m0-otel-20260909, then re-query app_payment_transactions_total and payment-api span error rates for the same window.
Verify with the platform owner whether the payment-api pod running at 13:45 UTC differed from payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-98kcz, since the retained objects postdate the incident.
